synopsis: Data lineage records data origins and transformations, while the independence rule requires that evidence used to judge a system played no part in building or tuning it; production-detector outputs cannot serve as independent ground truth [f14471, f99]. Across braking-model calibration, simulation credibility and collision-mitigation tuning, the corpus requires separate development, validation and withheld confirmation or audit data, with whole sites, weather episodes, machine identities or scenario families held together rather than randomly splitting adjacent frames [f6170, f7589, f6992, f6990, f6991]. Audit failures must not feed back into tuning: examined cases used to change thresholds are contaminated, and a late safety-relevant threshold change requires new independent statistical confirmation for the affected claim [f6952, f6953, f14375]. For machine-learning validation and estimation, the stated rule requires real or physically independent data, different assets, sites, people and generators, and documented lineage; its cited ISO/PAS 8800:2024 connection is explicitly on-road evidence and expert opinion from a third-party summary, not direct off-road proof [f7100, f7101]. Reproducible evidence also needs immutable run manifests, versioned assets, checksums and controlled archival, alongside a dedicated data-pedigree workstream; privacy obligations remain unquantified, and technical access to supplier data does not necessarily confer simulation, sharing, retention or derivative-model rights [f11069, f10346, f1145, f10813].
